props.title: Love Don't Cost a Thing
props.initialSlug: Modern remake of Can't Buy Me Love with Nick Cannon

sections.content: Love Don't Cost a Thing reimagines the 1987 teen classic Can't Buy Me Love for a new generation, shifting the setting to an urban high school and centering on Nick Cannon as Alvin Johnson, a brilliant but socially awkward teen who makes a deal with the popular Christina Milian. The film maintains the core premise of its predecessor while incorporating early 2000s teen movie aesthetics seen in films like Save the Last Dance (2001) and Brown Sugar (2002). It's part of a wave of African-American led teen romantic comedies that emerged in this era, including Deliver Us from Eva (2003) and You Got Served (2004).

sections.content: The early 2000s saw a surge in teen movie remakes that updated classic narratives for contemporary audiences. Beyond Love Don't Cost a Thing, films like Get Over It (2001) reimagined Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, while 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) modernized The Taming of the Shrew. These films shared common themes about social hierarchies, authenticity, and the price of popularity, but added modern music, fashion, and cultural references to connect with millennial viewers. SUBHEAD: Teen Romance Reimagined

Nick Cannon's performance draws from both Patrick Dempsey's original portrayal and adds elements reminiscent of other awkward-teen-transformation stories like She's All That (1999) and Drive Me Crazy (1999). The film's soundtrack heavily features early 2000s R&B and hip-hop, marking a significant departure from the 80s pop of the original. This musical shift reflects similar contemporary teen films like Drumline (2002) and Coach Carter (2005), which integrated hip-hop culture into mainstream teen narratives.
